The test image shows a soybean stem split open longitudinally, revealing **brown/reddish-brown discoloration of the internal pith tissue**. The stem exterior remains green while the interior shows clear brownish discoloration.

Key observations:
- Longitudinal stem section showing internal pith
- Clear brown/orange-brown discoloration of pith tissue
- Green exterior stem with hairy surface intact
- No external lesions or mold visible

Comparing to the BSR reference: the symptom description matches precisely — "Brown discoloration of the stem pith" is the hallmark of Brown Stem Rot. The reference collage also shows split stems with internal discoloration. This is distinct from Sudden Death Syndrome (white pith) and from other diseases in this list that affect leaves/pods/roots primarily.
